summary.intent: Land a wave of monokl work: object-literal member blocks (PR #68), conceptual-query ranking (PR #69), a decision-log catch-up (PR #67), and then address the review findings against the class-member blocks PR (#66).
summary.outcome: Three PRs were opened (#67, #68, #69) with local gates green. The review confirmed ownership bugs in #66's pipeline; these were fixed test-first with portion-aware ownership, the full gate passed (693 tests, 97.54%), harness results were unchanged, and the fix was committed for pushing to #66's branch.

repo: Stacked PRs: #68 and #69 are based on feat/member-blocks-class-methods (#66), while #67 is based on main. Fixes to #66 are pushed to its branch.
Local gate recipes: just lint, test, doc-check, deny, machete, check-drift, changesets, coverage, typos. They are run before declaring a PR ready.
Adding a SymbolKind variant forces edits in rank/boost.rs, rank/mod.rs, rank/proptests.rs, output/agent.rs and types.rs, so object literals render as `variable` rather than `object`.
analysis/ts treats `export default function X` as SymbolKind::Other (boost x0.7) instead of Function. This hurts axios buildFullPath and dispatchRequest, and a unit test pins the behavior.
`module.exports = { ... }` produces no block in the extractor, so it is not covered by member splitting.
scripts/rg-compare.py on the stacked base predates member questions; the member-question harness must be taken from origin/eval/member-questions.

Pipeline owned_hits previously assigned ownership by line, giving a line to every non-nested block containing it. This caused spurious rows when sibling members share a line, when the object header and a member start share a line, and when a trailing comment follows a member's closing brace.

code.finding: owned_hits uses line-granular ownership, which credits hits to the wrong sibling member. It was changed to portion-aware ownership so a hit is credited only to a block whose text contains the matched portion.
The no-line-credited-to-two-blocks property was rewritten to also cover the 'own text matches' filter and its fallback.
The API fixture has no shared lines, so the original no-double-credit test passed without any guard. New tests for shared-line and trailing-comment cases failed before the fix and passed after.

workflow: Test-first confirmation: new tests were run to confirm they fail before the fix (two were red, two were guards that already held).
Behavior changes were verified with a before/after rg-compare harness covering hit@3, declaration_in_output, question recall, output bytes and search time.
Parallel subagent workflows were used for independent PRs plus a review agent, with findings reproduced against real CLI output before fixing.
Honest reporting: unverifiable numbers were dropped from the decision log, and untested areas were stated explicitly.

friction: The task-notification result was truncated, so the full review findings had to be re-read from the output file.
The proptests.rs rewrite needed a second pass after the first test run failed.
A test in members.rs needed updating after the ownership change altered expected output.
CI was still pending on all the PRs at the time of the summary.
Edits to files outside the allowed set (pipeline/mod.rs test order, tests/cli.rs, tests/members.rs, architecture docs) were needed for the ranking change.
open_items: Add a SymbolKind::Object variant so parents render as `object X`. This is a one-variant follow-up touching rank/boost.rs, rank/mod.rs, rank/proptests.rs, output/agent.rs and types.rs.
Fix analysis/ts so `export default function` is classed Function, which would fix the axios misses buildFullPath and dispatchRequest.
Remaining ranking misses: zod 'safe parse result' (rank 5) and the member question 'registry has schema'.
The remaining review findings, including the trailing-comment one, were truncated from the summary and need to be confirmed as addressed.
Push the ownership fix to #66's branch, then confirm CI on #66-#69 and restack as needed.
Update scripts/rg-compare.py on the stacked base to include member questions.
